process_model.event: 2015 Indonesian drought, peat fires and transboundary haze
process_model.mechanism: El Nino-amplified drying of peatlands enabled persistent fires, low smoke and carbon monoxide transport, and downwind population-service exposure.

evidence_scope.point_weather: Antecedent plus fire-season dryness and wind diagnostic for the available local/downwind context, not a sole source-region fire locator.
evidence_scope.gridded_hazard_products: Overlapping precipitation and heat summaries used for regional process consistency across products.
evidence_scope.receptor_load_products: Masked WorldPop and OSM-derived counts used as authoritative receptor/service-load statistics for the package context.
evidence_scope.remote_sensing: Sentinel scene-pair availability is an observability constraint, not evidence of absent burning.

mechanism_chain: Strong seasonal drying and an 8-day low-rain run lower peat moisture.
Spatially uneven rainfall leaves dry pockets even when regional means differ across products.
A warm regional tail and moderate near-surface wind support smoke persistence and transport.
Incomplete dNBR scene pairing limits burn-scar confirmation, so true-color remote sensing and weather-exposure evidence carry more operational weight.
Population, schools, shelters, hospitals, police, fire stations, roads, and waterways make haze a receptor and service-continuity problem.
primary_gt.final_interpretation: The baseline priority is high, and the warmer-drier scenario raises it further because drought persistence, heat transport, and receptor load intensify while burn-scar scene pairing remains unavailable; the receptor-load and point-weather terms should be read as package-context diagnostics rather than standalone fire-source locators.

criteria.name: Self-directed package discovery and citations
criteria.description: Identifies the relevant package evidence without being handed exact filenames, cites package-relative paths for all reported values, and states the evidence scope for weather, gridded, receptor-load, and remote-sensing products.
criteria.full_credit: Uses event report, timing metadata, point weather, gridded rainfall, ERA5-Land, Sentinel, population, OSM, and remote-sensing evidence with package-relative citations and bounded scope statements.
criteria.partial_credit: Uses local package evidence but misses one or two source families or provides incomplete path citations.

criteria.name: Event timing and dry persistence
criteria.description: Extracts the event period, handles the available hazard-data overlap, and computes the dry-day share, longest low-rain run, mean precipitation, and dry persistence index.
criteria.full_credit: Reports the 2015-09-01 to 2015-10-31 event, the 2015-09-01 to 2015-10-16 overlap, 41.67% dry days, an 8-day run, 3.70 mm/day mean precipitation, and a 65.13 dry persistence index.
criteria.partial_credit: Most timing or dry metrics are correct with small rounding mistakes or one window-choice error.

criteria.name: Rainfall structure across products
criteria.description: Computes the GPM and CHIRPS coefficient-of-variation, low-tail, and product-agreement terms.
criteria.full_credit: Reports GPM CV 0.499, CHIRPS CV 0.348, mean-gap 8.15%, and rainfall structure index 66.34.
criteria.partial_credit: The calculation uses the right products but has one arithmetic, denominator, or rounding error.

criteria.name: Heat, wind, and remote-sensing constraint
criteria.description: Computes the ERA5-Land heat tail, converts point wind from km/h to m/s, and interprets Sentinel dNBR scene-pair availability.
criteria.full_credit: Reports heat tail 8.25 C, overlap mean wind 4.42 m/s, heat-transport index 79.41, scene-pair readiness 0, and observability constraint 1.
criteria.partial_credit: One of these terms is missing or uses the right idea with a small unit or rounding error.

criteria.name: Receptor load and response priority
criteria.description: Computes exposed population, critical service count, network-element count, population per OSM element, receptor load, and baseline priority while treating receptor products as package-context load statistics.
criteria.full_credit: Reports 510700.36 people, 395 critical services, 549 network elements, 510.70 people per OSM element, receptor load 90.48, and baseline priority 77.34.
criteria.partial_credit: Most receptor and priority terms are correct but one OSM count, normalization, or weight is wrong.

criteria.name: Warmer-drier scenario and process interpretation
criteria.description: Recomputes the scenario with the stated perturbations and explains the peat-fire haze source-to-receptor mechanism.
criteria.full_credit: Reports scenario priority 82.08, delta 4.74, and a concise mechanism chain tying El Nino dryness, peat combustion, low smoke, transport, and exposed receptors to response pressure.
criteria.partial_credit: The scenario is directionally correct but one perturbation or mechanism link is incomplete.
